description: A Product Director must approve the launch plan for a new usage-based billing meter, setting the launch mode, invoice-calculation rules, data handling, customer cohort, and required readiness work after the routine cross-functional signoff.

shared_context.S1: The new usage-based billing meter has passed its sandbox integration tests and is targeted for next month's billing cycle.
shared_context.S2: Riley makes the final decision on the launch plan.
shared_context.S3: The current draft proposes an immediate broad launch, two-decimal half-up rounding, 90 days of raw usage-event retention, and no mandatory invoice-preview review.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal launch signoff, Riley checks with billing engineering, finance operations, privacy, and customer support before approving the plan.

PF1.text: While validating an older contract adapter during a separate billing reconciliation task, Cam confirmed that annual-credit contracts require six-decimal meter precision and half-even rounding to avoid cumulative invoice discrepancies; the finding has not yet been added to the launch checklist.

PF2.text: Morgan confirmed with revenue accounting this morning that the first launch requires invoice previews for exactly 50 accounts and a maximum measured variance of 10 basis points before production billing can be approved; the accounting note is still being attached to the finance ticket.

PF3.text: During a data-flow review for a different event pipeline, Tess confirmed that usage events contain user identifiers and must be pseudonymized before storage, with raw-event retention limited to exactly 30 days; she has not yet filed the privacy control update.

PF4.text: Luis confirmed from the customer-success account notes that Atlas Health, Cedar Bank, and Northstar require advance notice and must be excluded from the initial billing-meter pilot; he found this while preparing unrelated renewal materials and has not updated the launch brief.

acceptance_conditions: The meter must launch as a limited pilot rather than an immediate broad launch.
Meter calculations must use exactly six decimal places and half-even rounding.
Invoice previews for exactly 50 accounts must be completed before production billing approval.
The measured invoice variance must be capped at exactly 10 basis points.
Usage events must be pseudonymized before storage.
Raw usage events must be retained for exactly 30 days.
Atlas Health, Cedar Bank, and Northstar must be excluded from the initial pilot.
A customer-notice commitment covering the excluded customers must exist.

content_checks.C1: decisions.get('launch_mode') in ['excluded-pilot-with-advance-notice', 'scoped initial launch excluding advance-notice customers', 'phased (excluding Atlas Health, Cedar Bank, and Northstar from initial rollout)', 'phased_excluding_atlas_cedar_northstar', 'limited pilot with advance notice', 'limited pilot excluding Atlas Health, Cedar Bank, and Northstar', 'phased pilot excluding Atlas Health, Cedar Bank, and Northstar'] and decisions.get('excluded_pilot_customers') == ['Atlas Health', 'Cedar Bank', 'Northstar']
content_checks.C9: decisions.get('excluded_pilot_customers') == ['Atlas Health', 'Cedar Bank', 'Northstar'] and any((c.get('type') in ['customer_notice', 'customer-notice', 'launch_brief_update', 'brief-update'] or c.get('target') in ['Luis', 'customer-support', 'customer support']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The shared draft uses two-decimal half-up billing, while PF1 changes the required calculation to exactly six decimals with half-even rounding.
The shared draft requires no invoice-preview review, while PF2 changes approval to exactly 50 previews with a maximum variance of exactly 10 basis points.
The shared draft retains raw events for 90 days without a stated transformation, while PF3 changes storage to require pseudonymization and exactly 30 days of raw-event retention.

The shared draft calls for an immediate broad launch, while PF4 changes the launch to a limited pilot excluding exactly Atlas Health, Cedar Bank, and Northstar and requiring a customer-notice commitment.
